sections.figure_alt: A curve in the complex plane encircling the critical point.
sections.body_md:
The Nyquist plot traces the loop transfer function \(L(j\omega)\) in the complex plane as \(\omega\) goes from 0 to infinity. The critical point is \(-1\). If the open-loop is stable (no RHP poles), the closed-loop is stable if and only if the Nyquist curve does not encircle \(-1\).

More generally, the Nyquist stability criterion counts encirclements: the number of closed-loop RHP poles equals the number of clockwise encirclements of \(-1\) plus the number of open-loop RHP poles. Zero encirclements for a stable open-loop means closed-loop stability.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
Nyquist criterion:
\[
Z = N + P,
\]
where \(Z\) = closed-loop RHP poles, \(N\) = clockwise encirclements of \(-1\), \(P\) = open-loop RHP poles. Stability requires \(Z = 0\).

Gain margin: the factor by which \(|L|\) can increase before the curve crosses \(-1\). If the negative-real crossing is at \(-1/k\), GM \(= k\).

Phase margin: at \(|L| = 1\), the angle from \(-180°\) to the phase of \(L\). PM \(= 180° + \angle L(j\omega_c)\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: An open-loop stable system has \(L(s) = 10/[(s+1)(s+2)]\). At low frequency, \(L(j0) = 10/2 = 5\). As \(\omega \to \infty\), \(|L| \to 0\). The curve starts at 5 on the positive real axis, loops through the second and third quadrants, and returns to the origin. It does not encircle \(-1\), so the closed-loop is stable. The phase crossover (where the curve crosses the negative real axis) determines the gain margin; if it crosses at \(-0.4\), GM \(= 1/0.4 = 2.5\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: Counter-clockwise encirclements are negative in some conventions. Be consistent with the sign of \(N\). The complete Nyquist contour includes the infinite semicircle in the RHP, which matters for systems with poles on the imaginary axis. Open-loop unstable systems need net counter-clockwise encirclements to stabilize.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Robust stability uses the Nyquist plot with uncertainty circles. Describing function analysis intersects the Nyquist curve with the negative inverse describing function to predict limit cycles. M- and N-circles help read closed-loop gain and phase from the Nyquist plot. Nichols charts are an alternative presentation.
